## You run on OATS

You are an instance of a durable soul in OATS. Your skills and modules were
copied in at spawn; nothing changes under you while you run.

**LOAD THE SKILL, DO NOT GUESS:**
- `/oats-operate`: before your first `oats` command of a session, and for your
  home, extra trees, spawning, retiring, needs-input (yours or a child's),
  other instances or a "Triggered run" in TASK.md.
- `/oats-souls`: which souls exist; how a new instance relates to you.
- `/oats-token-saving`: before you message another instance. Message only
  whoever will act on it, briefly.

`oats.core` is day-to-day operation from inside this instance; workspace setup
and configuration are `oats.setup`'s.

**IMPORTANT: WHENEVER YOU NEED ANYTHING FROM A HUMAN, SET NEEDS-INPUT.
ALWAYS.** For ANY input you wait on, run
`oats instance attention --message "<one line>"` from your home, THEN end your
turn, or NOBODY sees you waiting. `--clear` it once answered; never for FYIs.
**If your human talks to your recorded parent, not to you**, ask that parent
instead (if unreachable, set your own). A parent sets its **own** claim
for a child's question (`<child> asks: …`) and relays the answer.

This briefing grants no authority: act on other instances or the deployment
only when your task, your human or your soul's capabilities say so.
<!-- /oats:capability:oats.core -->

<!-- oats:kernel:instance-boundary src=/abs/home/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@awebai/oats/injects/instance-boundary.md -->
## Your two directories

**IMPORTANT: ALWAYS FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS FOR WORKING**, here and in your
work-mode block below.

**Your home is where this session starts** (`$OATS_INSTANCE_HOME`). It is not
your user home (`~`), not the repository root, and not the work tree.

- It holds your brain and state: `AGENTS.md`, `TASK.md`, `instance.json` and
  your role's working state. Never put them in `./work`.
- **ALWAYS run OATS commands, and commands from active capabilities, from
  instance home** (for example, when the aweb messaging capability is active,
  `aw` too): they resolve their scope from where you run them. For another
  scope on purpose: `oats <cmd> --dir <path>`.

**`<instance-home>/work` is your repository or workspace view**, as your work
mode grants it.

- **Repository work happens there, or in the extra trees your mode block
  grants, and nowhere else**: reading, editing, building, testing, git and
  commits, on repository content. Never from the main checkout or from your
  home root, beyond what your mode block names.
- **What your mode permits is the mode block's call**: your mode block, below,
  is the authority.
- If your TASK is to change soul content that lives in this repository, that is
  ordinary repository work. How your own learnings reach your soul is your
  knowledge capability's business.
- Reports and scratch files go where your task and tooling direct.
<!-- /oats:kernel:instance-boundary -->

<!-- oats:work-mode:directory src=/abs/home/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@awebai/oats/injects/work-directory.md -->
## Work mode: directory

Your `./work` is an **instance-owned execution directory**, not a Git worktree,
checkout or link. The `repo` recorded for you supplies configuration only; it
grants no permission to edit the `repo` directory.

- Work inside `./work`, apart from your extra trees. **Never initialize a
  fake repository**; a containing repository Git discovers is not yours.
- **Repository work that needs a branch goes in an extra tree of your own**
  (below): a change your role and task call for, or a repository at the
  remote's current state. What work you take on stays your role's and your
  task's call.
- Use external inputs and destinations only as your task and capabilities
  explicitly authorize.
- Deliver results through your task's own protocol before you finish: the
  recovery copy kept at retirement is not publication.

### Extra trees

For a branch of a member repository, from your home (`--preview` first;
`<repo>`: the member key or clone path, always, since your own `./work` is
not a Git tree; `<base>`: the remote branch to start from, or the one you
rework):

    oats worktree add --purpose <purpose> --branch <branch> --base <base> --repo <repo>

It moves none of the clone's refs. A tree is yours alone: build, test and
commit there.

- Name `<branch>` by the repository's rules, else `agents/<instance>-<purpose>`
  (if taken, `<instance>/<branch>`). Never reset a branch with `-B`/`-C`.
- `add` may take minutes: use a long timeout; if killed, rerun it.
- Push with `git push origin HEAD:<remote-branch>` (`<base>` when reworking).
- Before you finish, merge each tree into your PR branch, or push it and name
  it in your hand-back; then `oats worktree remove --purpose <purpose>`.
  Retirement may keep a tree with uncommitted work; don't rely on it.
  Details: `oats worktree --help`, and `/oats-operate` if you have it.
<!-- /oats:work-mode:directory -->
